articles.headline: Parma part ways with ex-Arsenal assistant Carlos Cuesta
articles.description: Parma parted ways with coach Carlos Cuesta on Sunday after winning only one of their opening five Serie A matches.
articles.headlineJa: パルマ、元アーセナル助監督のカルロス・クエスタ氏と契約解除
articles.descriptionJa: パルマはセリエA開幕5試合でわずか1勝にとどまり、日曜日にカルロス・クエスタ監督と解任・退任の道を歩むこととなった。
articles.body:
Parma parted ways with coach Carlos Cuesta on Sunday after winning only one of their opening five Serie A matches.

The club said Cuesta "has been relieved of his duty" and that "following an internal discussion between the club and coach, it was agreed that the conditions in order to continue this working relationship and the advancement of the sporting project, were not being met. Both parties came to a mutual agreement."

- Goals galore! Why Barça's start to season is best in Europe's top leagues for almost 100 years

- Udinese sign former Real Madrid defender Alaba

- Havertz back at Arsenal for injury treatment

A replacement was not immediately named.

Parma beat Genoa last weekend but only have four points.

Cuesta became the youngest manager in Europe's top five leagues, and the youngest Serie A manager in almost a century, when he was appointed by Parma in June 2025 at the age of 29. He had previously spent five years as assistant to Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta.

Having decided at a young age that his future lay in coaching rather than playing, Cuesta was given his first chance at Atlético Madrid with their underage teams and after four years there, went travelling Europe to study coaching methods.

It was during this period that Cuesta met Arteta, then part of Pep Guardiola's coaching staff at Manchester City, and after a two-year spell with Juventus' youth academy, Cuesta joined Arsenal in 2020.

He guided Parma to a 13th-place finish last season.

It's the third coaching change in Serie A this season after Paolo Vanoli replaced Fabio Grosso at Fiorentina and Raffaele Palladino replaced Domenico Tedesco at Bologna.

Parma's next match is at Serie A champions Inter Milan on Oct. 10 after the international break.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: LaLiga chief Javier Tebas criticises Man City's alleged rule breaches: 'Equal rules for all'
articles.description: LaLiga president Javier Tebas has said Manchester City legal battle against the Premier League shows why "equal rules for all" are essential.
articles.headlineJa: ラ・リーガのテバス会長、マンCのルール違反疑惑を批判：「すべての人に平等なルールを」
articles.descriptionJa: ラ・リーガのハビエル・テバス会長は、マンチェスター・シティのプレミアリーグに対する法的闘争が、なぜ「すべての人に平等なルール」が不可欠であるかを示していると語った。
articles.body:
LaLiga president Javier Tebas has said Manchester City legal battle against the Premier League shows why "equal rules for all" are essential to protect football's integrity and sustainability.

ESPN reported on Friday that a source has confirmed City are expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League.

In a statement, City didn't deny the guilty verdicts and said that the process "remains ongoing."

When contacted by ESPN on Friday, the Premier League said it wouldn't comment on a "private and confidential process."

The Athletic first reported Friday that City had been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges by an independent panel.

- Ogden: Man City verdict will leave a stain and stench on a Premier League era

In 2020, Man City succeeded in overturning a two-year European competition ban from UEFA at the Court of Arbitration, after being found to have breached the governing body's Financial Fair Play (FFP) rule.

Tebas had previously spoken out against "so-called financial doping in European football".

In a lengthy post on X, Tebas reflected on those statements he had given during the Soccerex event, which had been held in Manchester during September 2017.

Tebas also called the CAS ruling a "deeply misguided decision" which was "extraordinarily damaging to the credibility of European football's economic control system" and again stressed the same rules must apply to all clubs.

"Economic sustainability is not bureaucracy. Financial control is not a whim," he said.

"And arguing that clubs should compete fundamentally with the resources they are able to generate doesn't mean being against any specific club either. It's about defending a model.

"A model in which sporting success doesn't depend on who has the most powerful financial backing behind them, but on who manages best, generates more resources, builds better teams, and respects the same rules as everyone else.

"Defending this position has cost me a lot of criticism and not a few headaches. But I still think exactly the same as I did in Manchester in 2017.

"There are principles worth defending, even if they come at a cost. And this one, for me, is one of them.

- Man City chairman on club's Premier League charges case: 'Nothing has changed'

"Now, almost nine years after those words at Soccerex, an independent Premier League commission has deemed 114 of the 115 financial breaches charged against Manchester City proven, according to the published reports.

"There's still a way to go. The sanction remains to be known, and the process isn't over. But what's happened once again shows why economic control, transparency, and equal rules for all are essential to protect the integrity and sustainability of football."

"We will keep defending those principles. Just like in 2017."

Information from PA contributed to this story.

articles.headline: NFL Week 3's best arrivals, led by Stefon Diggs
articles.description: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
articles.headlineJa: ステフォン・ディグスをはじめとする、NFL第3週のベスト・会場入りファッション
articles.descriptionJa: NFLのスター選手たちは、試合当日のスタジアム入りを毎週恒例のファッションショーへと変え続けている。
articles.body:
The official start of fall means it's fit season, when players start dominating the gameday tunnels with eye-popping jackets, sweaters and pants.

Last week, the Philadelphia Eagles played a blazing hot game in Nashville that had players' cleats melting with with temperatures of up to 157 degrees Fahrenheit on the turf. 

Hopefully this week is the start of a heat decline with more cloudier 50-to-75 degree days ahead to allow players to comfortably show off their fits.

To kick off Week 3, Green Bay Packers quarterbacks Jordan Love and Tyrod Taylor rocked my two favorite outfits of the Thursday primetime slate.

Love came in shining -- literally -- with a Public School New York x KAY jewelry collaboration jacket: the definition of a statement piece.

Meanwhile, Taylor's Dries Van Noten sweater is the perfect kickoff to fall -- warm but fashion-forward. There are so many fabric design details within this one piece, showing the value of layers.

As always, Sunday is where the big show begins. Here are Week 3 fits that caught our eye:

Sunday's best

From Stefon Diggs' black jacket covered in NBA throwback logo patches, to Malik Nabers' custom "H1M" pendant, players brought plenty of style and personality ahead of the early slate. 

Thursday night fashion

The Green Bay Packers host the Atlanta Falcons to kick off Week 3's slate, and quarterback Jordan Love entered the home opener in style, pairing an oversize studded leather pullover with black trousers, a crisp white shirt and black tie. He completed the look with dark sunglasses and a checkered duffel bag.

articles.headline: 2027 NFL draft questions, latest intel, risers, CFB standouts
articles.description: Will Colin Simmons be the runaway top edge for 2027? How early could Jadan Baugh get picked in April? Here's NFL draft spin off Week 4 of the CFB season.
articles.headlineJa: 2027年NFLドラフトの疑問、最新情報、評価急上昇選手、CFBの注目選手
articles.descriptionJa: コリン・シモンズは2027年のダントツのトップエッジラッシャーとなるのか？ ジェイダン・ボーは4月にどれほど早い順位で指名される可能性があるのか？ カレッジフットボール（CFB）シーズン第4週から得られたNFLドラフトの展望をお届けする。
articles.body:
The biggest storylines coming out of Week 4 of the 2026 college football season include Texas surviving against Tennessee behind five sacks from Colin Simmons, Florida knocking off Ole Miss after Jadan Baugh scored three TDs, Oregon getting past USC even after Dante Moore was forced out of the game and Iowa coming back to top Michigan on the final play. Mississippi State also defeated Missouri on a big Kamario Taylor day, Wake Forest upset Louisville and Wisconsin edged Penn State.

What about the top 2027 NFL draft prospects? Who stood out? Yes, the draft is still about seven months away, but our analysts are always looking down the road, taking early notes on top players and starting to stack their rankings for an exciting class.

With that in mind, Mel Kiper Jr. and Jordan Reid will size up CFB action through a draft-centric lens on Sundays all season long. They are answering lingering questions on the best 2027 prospects, sharing insights from scouts, picking out risers to watch and pulling back the curtain on their evaluation process. Here is what they saw and heard through Week 4.

Jump to:

Week 4 | Week 3 | Week 2

Sept. 27

Is Colin Simmons the runaway top edge rusher in this class?

Reid: The scouting trail continued for me this week in Knoxville, Tennessee, where I had a front-row seat for Simmons' five-sack performance against the Vols. It tied the Texas single-game record set in 1990. Outside of an excessive sack celebration from Simmons, it was one of the best defensive performances that I've ever seen. At 6-foot-3 and 246 pounds, his combination of upfield burst and closing speed make it challenging for blockers to keep pace with him. Most impressive was how many different spots he got pressure from. Simmons not only rushed from both edges but also reduced down inside on late downs and wreaked havoc from there, as well.

I got to see South Carolina's Dylan Stewart last week against Mississippi State, and he should be a top pick, too. It's likely going to be a "traits against production" debate between the two; Stewart is the more explosive athlete with better size (6-foot-5, 250 pounds), but Simmons continues to produce at an elite level (seven sacks this season). But yes ... Simmons is the clear top player at the position at this point in the season.

What's the earliest Jadan Baugh could come off the board if he keeps this up?

Reid: A tough and rugged runner at 6-foot-1 and 225 pounds, Baugh has the makings of a top-20 pick. I think the Florida standout could go in the teens, as there are a lot of NFL teams that need a true RB1.

How good has Baugh been? Per ESPN Research, he became only the second player in the past 20 seasons with at least 100 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns in each of the first four games of a season, joining Leonard Fournette (2015). articles.headline: Jets without WR Adonai Mitchell (finger) vs. Lions
articles.description: Jets wide receiver Adonai Mitchell is inactive Sunday because of a finger injury.
articles.headlineJa: ジェッツ、ライオンズ戦でWRアドナイ・ミッチェルが指の負傷により欠場
articles.descriptionJa: ジェッツのワイドレシーバー（WR）アドナイ・ミッチェルは、指の負傷のため日曜日の試合を出場登録外となっています。
articles.body:
DETROIT -- The New York Jets' injury-riddled receiving corps took another hit Sunday with the news that Adonai Mitchell, their most-targeted player last week, was declared inactive with a finger injury.

This means Garrett Wilson and Isaiah Williams will be their top two wideouts Sunday against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field. Their three backups, none of whom were on the roster at the start of the season, were added this week to the active roster.

That group is led by veteran Sterling Shepard, who arrived only two weeks ago on the practice squad. The others are Malik McClain, an undrafted rookie, and first-year player Jamaal Pritchett. Both will make their NFL debut.

Mitchell was injured Thursday when he caught a finger in a teammate's jersey during practice. He was limited on Friday and listed as questionable.

Coach Aaron Glenn claimed the finger isn't fractured, yet Mitchell was spotted Friday with a heavy wrap on his right hand, with his index and middle fingers splinted.

Mitchell, their top vertical threat, has been targeted a team-high 15 times. He has nine receptions for 123 yards.

The Jets have three receivers on injured reserve -- first-round pick Omar Cooper Jr, Tim Patrick and Arian Smith. 

The Jets also are without starting tight end Mason Taylor (thumb).

articles.description: The Bulls have traded Rob Dillingham to the Hornets for Buddy Hield and cash.
articles.headlineJa: ブルズ、バディ・ヒールドと金銭とのトレードでロブ・ディリンガムをホーネッツへ放出
articles.descriptionJa: ブルズは、バディ・ヒールドおよび金銭とのトレードでロブ・ディリンガムをホーネッツに放出した。
articles.body:
The Chicago Bulls have traded Rob Dillingham to the Charlotte Hornets for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Sunday.

Dillingham, the No. 8 pick in the 2024 NBA draft and still just 21 years old, was moved less than a year after landing in Chicago at the trade deadline last season. He appeared in 30 games for the Bulls, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists.

He could have a chance for a larger role in Charlotte, which traded longtime starting guard LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves earlier this offseason. Dillingham also joins the Hornets after Charlotte announced Friday that second-year guard Kon Knueppel has been sidelined with a hamstring injury.

The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the deal. 

Hield spent less than a week with the Hornets, who acquired the veteran sharpshooter from the Atlanta Hawks for Dorian Finney-Smith. Hield, known as a positive and high-energy player, has history with Bulls executive vice president Bryson Graham from their time together in New Orleans. 

Dillingham has one more year via a team option on his rookie contract before hitting restricted free agency in the summer of 2028. Hield has a player option worth around $10 million for the 2027-28 season.
